To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) arts marketing research has been dominated by the marketing mix, (ii) the marketing mix has been shown to be ineffective for contemporary arts marketing, and (iii) the arts marketing mix needs to be replaced by an audience engagement mix.

1) the marketing mix, and in particular the 4P model is not fit for purpose in the twenty first century arts sector; 2) arts marketing should be reconfigured to reflect contemporary philosophies of audience engagement and audience development; 3) audience engagement and audience enrichment are the key concepts that should be central to contemporary arts marketing practice.

the traditional marketing mix is no longer fit for the contemporary arts marketing context and that audience engagement and audience enrichment should replace audience acquisition and audience satisfaction as the key objectives of arts marketing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a critical re-examination of the arts marketing field, its theoretical and conceptual underpinning, its current practices and its future potential.
the following questions: How can arts marketing be redefined to reflect the conceptual and philosophical evolution of the field?

a fundamental reconfiguration in arts marketing research, practice, and education, which will help arts organisations to better understand their audience, and to develop more appropriate and effective strategies for audience engagement and enrichment in the twenty first century.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

it is time for the performing arts industry and the arts marketing discipline to reassert the fundamental role of the arts and humanities research in tailoring arts organisations back to their creative and not for profits roots.
arts marketing has become an increasingly complex and sophisticated discipline, which is in need of a new paradigm to reflect its current conceptual and practical evolution.
it is time for arts marketing to move on from the traditional marketing mix, and to embrace a new paradigm of audience centred engagement and enrichment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are arguing that arts marketing needs to be reconfigured as a form of audience enrichment and engagement rather than as a form of consumer consumption.
we have argued that the marketing of the arts is in need of fundamental reconfiguration.
the chapter presents a critical review of arts marketing scholarship and practice in light of the current challenges faced by the performing arts industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traditional marketing mix is not fit to serve the purpose of arts organisations that are increasingly concerned with audience engagement and enrichment rather than audience consumption.
the marketing of the arts is a social process, and not a commercial one.
the arts marketing concept is not a one-size fits all solution, but rather a set of principles that can be adapted to the needs and circumstances of individual arts organisations.
